title: Node lander self-heals a dirty runtime-metadata tree instead of looping BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE
description:
MEASURED LIVE (UnAI, 2026-09-17): goal-b2cc3b54's FIRST node.deliver looped ~5 min refusing REPOSITORY_DELIVERY_BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE. Root cause: the node lander's baseline() (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/repository-delivery-runtime.ts:128-141) calls git.observe(workspace) and returns null the moment ANY entry is dirty, logging e.g. `[lander] <node>: TRACKED_RUNTIME_METADATA_DIRTY (1 tracked runtime metadata path(s) changed: [".moe-next/start.ps1"] ...)`. node.deliver then refuses BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE and the wrapper auto-retries FOREVER ("automatic retry after <ts>") until a human checkpoints the tree. It only unblocked when the operator manually `git commit`ed the one dirty path.

The dirty path was `.moe-next/start.ps1`, edited earlier this session to add `--operator-stdin`. Two compounding facts:
1. `.moe-next/start.ps1` is TRACKED, yet `.moe-next` is in .gitignore — a tracked file inside an ignored dir. The runtime-metadata git-exclude work (PR#46 era) never `git rm --cached`ed it, so any edit to it dirties the tree.
2. The lander treats a dirty tracked runtime-metadata path as a hard baseline refusal, with no self-heal — so a routine operator edit to a runtime file wedges ALL node execution behind a human.

OWNER DIRECTION (2026-09-17): "instead of the dirty cycle, the node should commit what's needed or stash." i.e. the lander should checkpoint/stash the dirty RUNTIME-METADATA paths itself rather than park behind a human.

DELIVERABLE OPTIONS (plan the leanest; likely BOTH — prevention + defense):
- (a) DEFENSE: before refusing, the lander auto-checkpoints (commit) or stashes dirty paths that are on the RUNTIME-METADATA allowlist only, then re-observes and proceeds. Scope is the crux: it must NEVER auto-commit product code — only the known runtime-metadata set (.moe-next/ runtime files). A dirty PRODUCT path must still block (that dirt is the operator's real work).
- (b) PREVENTION: untrack the runtime-metadata files that should not be in product history (`git rm --cached .moe-next/start.ps1` and siblings; keep them gitignored) so they never dirty the tree. Verify which .moe-next/* paths are tracked-but-ignored across a fresh project and the fixtures.

RE-MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING: what git.observe/the lander classifies as "tracked runtime metadata" (the allowlist), where that set is defined, and whether option (b) alone removes the class of dirt or the lander can still see other tracked runtime paths dirty.
definitionOfDone: A dirty TRACKED RUNTIME-METADATA path (e.g. an edited .moe-next/start.ps1) no longer wedges node.deliver: the lander either checkpoints/stashes it and records the baseline, or the path is untracked so it never dirties the tree. Verified against the exact live repro (edit start.ps1, claim a node, confirm BASELINE_RECORDED not BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE).

Scope fence proven: a dirty PRODUCT-CODE path STILL refuses the baseline (BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE) and is NOT auto-committed. Test asserts both arms — runtime-metadata dirt self-heals, product dirt still blocks — with the exact reason code/layer (global rail: assert the code, not just outcome).
If option (b): enumerate the .moe-next/* paths that are tracked while .moe-next is gitignored and untrack the runtime-metadata ones; confirm a fresh project bootstrap does not re-track them.

No infinite-retry stall path remains for the runtime-metadata dirty class: the wrapper reaches a delivered/executing node or a DISTINCT actionable refusal, not an endless REPOSITORY_DELIVERY_BASELINE_UNAVAILABLE loop.

implementationPlan.description: The self-heal, as a NEW focused module so neither existing file grows past its cap. Create apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-metadata-checkpoint.ts exporting one function, roughly `checkpointRuntimeMetadata({git, workspace, nodeRef, paths, clock}): Promise<{outcome: string; detail: string; ok: boolean}>`. Behaviour: (1) refuse `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_UNKNOWN_PATHS` if ANY supplied path is not classified as Moe runtime metadata -- this is the SCOPE FENCE and it must be enforced HERE, in production, not merely relied upon from the caller. Do NOT reimplement the classifier: export `isMoeMetadata` from git-landing-port.ts and import it, so the fence and the observer can never disagree (global rail: a property is asserted against the production surface, never a helper that reimplements it). (2) Call the EXISTING `git.commit(workspace, paths, message)` -- never write new git plumbing; it already stages by explicit nul-delimited pathspec under LANDER_IDENTITY, which is what keeps epic rail 3 (no `git add -A`, no stash, no reset) satisfied. Owner direction was "commit what's needed or stash": COMMIT is chosen and STASH is forbidden by epic rail 3, so a stash path must not be written. (3) Commit message names what happened and why in plain words -- that the node runtime checkpointed pre-existing runtime-metadata changes so execution could proceed, naming the node -- because this commit lands in the OPERATOR'S history and must be self-explaining and revertable. (4) On commit failure return `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_FAILED` carrying git's stderr tail. (5) Re-observe; if metadata is STILL dirty return the DISTINCT `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINT_INEFFECTIVE` rather than looping -- a silent re-loop here would just relocate the bug. On success return `RUNTIME_METADATA_CHECKPOINTED` carrying the count and the commit sha. Never log or embed a credential. Also create the one-line bridge apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/runtime-metadata-checkpoint.js containing exactly `export * from "./runtime-metadata-checkpoint.ts";` -- the orchestrator directory has 94 such bridges for 96 sources and an import will not resolve without it.
